title: No sin antes: reconocer un paso previo necesario

sections.content: No sin antes (not without first) acknowledges that something happened only after going through a difficult or necessary prior step -- useful for historical narration that wants to note the cost or process behind an outcome, not just announce the outcome itself. It's followed by an infinitive. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El gobierno sandinista aceptó celebrar elecciones libres, no sin antes enfrentar años de guerra y una profunda crisis interna.
items.english: The Sandinista government agreed to hold free elections, not without first facing years of war and a deep internal crisis.

items.spanish: Guatemala fue el último país en alcanzar la paz, no sin antes atravesar treinta y seis años de conflicto.
items.english: Guatemala was the last country to reach peace, not without first going through thirty-six years of conflict.

items.spanish: Ambas partes llegaron a un acuerdo, no sin antes negociar durante meses sobre los puntos más difíciles.
items.english: Both sides reached an agreement, not without first negotiating for months over the most difficult points.

items.spanish: El FMLN se convirtió en un partido político legal, no sin antes deponer completamente las armas.
items.english: The FMLN became a legal political party, not without first fully laying down its weapons.

sections.content: No sin antes always sits after the main clause describing the final outcome, then looks back at what had to happen first -- it doesn't work at the start of a sentence the way antes de does.
